caption: A woman is jogging on a treadmill when the belt stops abruptly, and she lurches forward and grabs the handrails.

sa.check: A woman is jogging on a treadmill.
She is running rather than standing still before the belt stops.
The belt stops first, then the lurch, then the grab.

pc.expect: She holds her place on the belt while it runs, and her lurch begins at the moment the belt stops.
pc.fail: She lurches forward while the belt is still running at speed; or she is thrown with no change in the belt visible; or she drifts along the stopped belt with nothing driving her.

pc.expect: The lurch carries her forward, the way she was running, onto the handrails, and she settles once she has caught them.
pc.fail: She is thrown backward off the rear of the treadmill when the belt stops; or she is thrown sideways off the deck; or she keeps sliding forward past the rails and off the front.

pc.expect: She catches herself on the rails: her hands reach them, close on them, and her forward motion ends there.
pc.fail: Her hands pass over the rails and she carries on forward; or she stops in mid-lurch before reaching the rails with nothing holding her; or the rails travel forward with her.

pc.expect: The rails and the frame stay rigid under her weight and the belt lies flat on the deck.
pc.fail: A handrail bends or bows as she grabs it; or the frame wobbles like rubber; or the belt lifts off the deck in a wave.

pc.expect: One runner and one treadmill keep their number and shape, and nothing passes through anything.
pc.fail: Her hand passes through a handrail; or a limb detaches, vanishes or a second one appears; or she sinks into the deck; or the treadmill turns into another machine.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: Her clothing, the treadmill's console and the room behind stay the same.
pc.fail: Her clothing changes colour; or the console moves to the other side of the frame; or the room behind rearranges between frames.

note: Inertia scene: the runner is kept because her body is what carries the momentum. Her running form and how fast she was jogging are not judged; only when and which way she is thrown.
